stem.en: Under a microscope, some yeast cells carry a smaller round bulge on one side. What is the bulge?

text.en: A spore that landed on the cell from the air

feedback.en: A spore would be loose. This bulge grows out of the cell itself.

text.en: A new cell growing out of the parent cell

feedback.en: Yes. It is a bud. It will enlarge and then separate.

text.en: A store of sugar that will burst out later

feedback.en: It is not a store of sugar. It is a young cell growing on its parent.

text.en: A second yeast cell that has bumped into it

feedback.en: Two loose cells would only touch. This bulge grows from the parent.

explanation.en: The bulge is a bud. It grows out of the parent cell, enlarges and then separates to live on its own. This is budding.

hints.en: Is the bulge loose, or is it growing from the cell?
What did the bud do next, in the steps?
